speaker: Doctor
text: You are the doctor. Please provide the patient's history or current symptoms so I can begin the examination.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Is there any history of maternal diabetes, polyhydramnios, or consanguinity during the pregnancy?
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray demonstrates a 'double bubble' sign, which is indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray shows a double bubble sign with no distal gas, which is classic for duodenal atresia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal atresia
